svg.title: GROUND: track work through resolution and handoff
svg.desc: Proposed resolution flow. Approved scope produces registered assignments, persisted research and evidence, targeted factual follow-up, design work, or prepared human decisions. Questions are not closed by relabeling, by a failed search, or by accepting a proposal whose required work remains undone. Completion checks original evidence and routes unresolved work to its responsible stage without dropping it. Existing human transition approvals remain required. The lower matrix identifies each tracked item's owner and closure evidence. C sharp resolution links are not yet defined.
svg.text: GROUND — every open item has a path to closure
PROPOSAL FOR REVIEW · Existing structures are reused. New closure relationships are not yet approved or implemented.
Conversation: approved work
Capabilities, platforms, scope, exclusions
Human decisions remain here.
One source of requirements.
Workflow: registered assignments
Stage → attempt → agent runs
Inputs and outputs are references.
No second work checklist.
Agents execute assigned work
Investigate before escalating.
Guard saves tool captures and exact results.
Successful work remains reusable.
Evaluate findings against the assigned requirement
Use original structured results and evidence, not a narrative report.
Supported answer → closure check. Missing answer → the responsible work.
Missing fact / conflicting evidence
Research agent investigates the question.
Use docs, SDK/source, RefLib or a probe
within the authorized scope.
Persist follow-up results and evidence.
Inconclusive evidence leaves it open.
Design or implementation work
Route to the stage that owns the work.
Give it the original findings by reference.
Name the question it must resolve.
A handoff is not a closure.
Do not force a design choice into GROUND.
A decision reserved for the human
Agent prepares the exact question, options,
recommendation, evidence and impact.
Human resolves the decision.
Record it once in Conversation.
Approval does not perform required work.
Close only against the question and its evidence
Does the result answer the original question for the affected platforms?
Is required follow-through complete, with supporting results?
If not: keep it open and route only the unfinished work.
Unfinished work only
No full-stage restart
Closure checks
Guard checks references
and required structure.
Stage review checks claims.
GROUND handoff: original results + linked resolutions
Research needed for the next decision is resolved, or the dependency stays blocked.
Later-stage work has an explicit destination; it remains open until done.
DESIGN receives the existing versioned result references.
Human time goes to prepared decisions and required approvals—not agent-readable facts or reconstructed reports.
All transition approvals still apply. Grouping related questions does not waive any approval or grant an exception.
What is tracked, where it lives, and what actually closes it
ITEM
EXISTING OWNER / FOLLOW-UP
CLOSURE — NOT JUST A STATUS CHANGE
Capability × selected platform
Conversation + Workflow assignment
An evidenced finding for that platform; or a human-approved scope change.
A failed search or empty list does not prove the platform is unsupported.
Search / read / probe
Tool capture + agent-run result
Actual response and outcome are retained. Failure remains visible.
Retry unfinished work; do not turn an error into “nothing found.”
Factual question / contradiction
Conversation.Issues → assigned follow-up
A resolving result answers the question and cites the original evidence.
If still unknown, it stays open; no Unsupported/default substitution.
Design question
Issue → DESIGN or responsible later stage
The required decision and resulting work satisfy the original requirement.
Routing the item forward is not evidence that it has been resolved.
Exception / scope-change proposal
Conversation.ProposedDecisions
Rejected: original requirement still applies. Accepted: exact change is recorded.
Any implementation and verification obligations remain tracked until done.
Interrupted or missing agent result
Workflow assignment → another agent run
A usable result for that assignment. Preserve other successful results.
A missing agent cannot vanish from the expected work.
Defect exposed by follow-up
Issue → owning code/test/rule stage
Correct the affected work and verify the behavior. Do not weaken expectations.
Correcting report prose alone does not repair a code or evidence defect.
No bypass: “unknown,” “deferred,” “not applicable,” and “approved” cannot silently satisfy an unmet requirement.
Still to define in C#: item identity, original-result reference, follow-up assignment reference and resolution evidence reference.
Issue and ProposedDecision currently lack those links. Extend their existing ownership; do not add another issue ledger.
This diagram proposes routing and closure criteria. It does not approve new automation, reviewers, exceptions or transition permissions.
